prs.title: fix(server): preserve plain JSON Schema in deprecated server.tool() overload
prs.author: stakeswky
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Plain JSON Schema objects passed to the deprecated server.tool() overload are not handled correctly (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Plain JSON Schema objects passed to the deprecated server.tool() overload are not handled correctly (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs address the same root issue from opposite angles. #1596 throws an error when it detects a nested-object shape (heuristic: `Object.values(firstArg).some(v => typeof v === 'object')`), treating plain JSON Schema as invalid input at the argument-parsing layer (~line 1024). #1617 instead detects plain JSON Schema early at the schema-rendering layer (~line 146) and passes it through unchanged, preserving backwards compatibility for callers already using raw JSON Schema with the deprecated overload. #1617 is preferable: it avoids a breaking change, correctly handles the deprecated use case, and the fix location (rendering layer) is more appropriate than #1596's argument-parsing heuristic, which could also incorrectly reject valid ToolAnnotations objects that happen to contain nested values.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs address the same root issue from opposite angles. #1596 throws an error when it detects a nested-object shape (heuristic: `Object.values(firstArg).some(v => typeof v === 'object')`), treating plain JSON Schema as invalid input at the argument-parsing layer (~line 1024). #1617 instead detects plain JSON Schema early at the schema-rendering layer (~line 146) and passes it through unchanged, preserving backwards compatibility for callers already using raw JSON Schema with the deprecated overload. #1617 is preferable: it avoids a breaking change, correctly handles the deprecated use case, and the fix location (rendering layer) is more appropriate than #1596's argument-parsing heuristic, which could also incorrectly reject valid ToolAnnotations objects that happen to contain nested values.
